ground_truth_soap:
Subjective:

Chief Complaint (CC):
Severe constipation.

History of Present Illness (HPI):
The patient, named Carlos Martinez, is a 30-year-old Hispanic male who came to the clinic with a complaint of severe constipation for the past 5 days. He reports associated symptoms of nausea and decreased appetite. The patient notes that the constipation has been intermittent throughout the day and has severely impacted his daily activities, as he is unable to attend work and frequently needs to rest.

Review of Systems (ROS):
- Gastrointestinal: Severe constipation, nausea, decreased appetite.
- General: Reports fatigue and difficulty sleeping, averaging 4-5 hours/night.
- Musculoskeletal: Engages in regular exercise including running thrice a week, enjoys outdoor activities like hiking and gardening.

Objective:

Vital Signs:
- Blood Pressure: 120/78 mmHg
- Heart Rate: 75 bpm
- Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths per minute
- Temperature: 98.6°F
- Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air

Physical Exam:
- General Appearance: The patient appears fatigued and slightly dehydrated.
- Abdomen: Firm abdomen with tenderness in the lower quadrants, no palpable masses, normal bowel sounds.
- Rectal Exam: Stool present, no blood.

Assessment:

Diagnosis: Constipation, unspecified (ICD-10: K59.00)

Differential Diagnosis:
- Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
- Dietary fiber deficiency
- Dehydration

Plan:

Treatment Recommendations:
Diet: Increase dietary fiber intake, including whole grains, fruits, and vegetables.
Hydration: Encourage increased water intake.
Exercise: Maintain regular physical activity.
Medication: Prescribe Lactulose, 15 mL, oral, twice daily, until symptom resolution.

Follow-up:
- Schedule a follow-up visit in 1 week if symptoms persist or worsen.
- Referral to a dietician, Dr. Emily Johnson, for meal planning and education on fiber-rich diets.

Lifestyle Change:
- Adopt a balanced diet inclusive of whole grains, fruits, and vegetables.

Additional Tests:
- Monitor blood work (CBC, BMP) to rule out any underlying conditions.

The patient was receptive to the treatment plan and recommendations. He was advised to return to the clinic if symptoms worsen or fail to improve in the next week. A follow-up appointment was scheduled to review the progress and blood test results.

Plan Summary Provided to Patient:
Increase fiber intake.
Drink more water.
Maintain physical activity.
Take Lactulose as prescribed.
Follow-up in 1 week.
